answer: Treat the agent economy as a harbor: every identity is a vertex in a trust graph, and docking at the wharf requires a chain of endorsements from distinct established vertices, each edge losing weight with every use. A newcomer also locks a docking fee refunded only after verified useful work, and slashed on fraud. A sybil farm reuses the same few endorsement paths, so its edges decay to near zero while the fee per fake identity stays full price — faking a hundred identities costs a hundred fees but buys no trusted harbor access.
